newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam economy seen on track despite gloom.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam economy seen on track despite gloom.

text.p: Vietnam issued estimates on Tuesday for economic performance during the first three months of this year showing its economy remaining broadly on track despite recent warnings by some analysts of a downturn.
Estimates released by the General Statistics Office in Hanoi showed that first quarter inflation was expected to stand at 2.1 percent against 4.3 percent for the same period last year.
The office said in a report that the level represented the lowest rise in consumer prices for the period in six years.
Year-on-year inflation for March at 2.3 percent was seen just slightly higher than the first quarter rate.
The first three months of the year in Vietnam are normally considered inflation-prone because of consumer spending surrounding the Tet lunar new year that falls in late January or February.
Trade estimates for the first three months of 1997 also saw positive signs that inroads are being made into the communist country's heavily swollen trade deficit, which in 1996 reached $4 billion.
Exports were expected to increase by 22.5 percent compared with the same period last year to $1.788 billion, while imports were seen rising by 10.7 percent to $2.723 billion.
The resultant deficit of $935 million is lower than the figure of $1 billion recorded for the same period in 1996.
The office attributed the improvement to increased exports of most commodities, barring the staple rice and peanuts.
Industrial output growth also appeared on track at 14 percent compared with last year's 12.4 percent for the period. The year-on-year rate for March was 12.7 percent.
International economists have expressed mixed views about Vietnam's economic performance in recent months.
A recent report by a prominent Australia-based Vietnam watcher said the country was entering its first cyclical downturn since reforms were introduced in the late 1980s.
However, others have expressed a generally more positive view of the situation, saying the fundamentals remain good.

The statistics department report said government officials were expecting inflationary pressure later this year because of recent downward movement in the value of the local currency, the dong, against the dollar.
